flagged.evidence: The proof says: “The matrix \(\rho(d)\) has rational entries and finite order \(|D|\).” Its order need only divide \(|D|\). For example, take \(C=D=C_2\), let \(d\) be its nonidentity generator, and let \(\rho\) be the trivial \(\mathbb Q\)-representation. Then \(\rho(d)=I\) has order \(1\), not \(|D|=2\).
